package.title: 100 MDCAT Human Physiology MCQs with Answers and Explanations

questions.question: Which statement best describes negative feedback in human physiology?
choices: A response reduces the original change that triggered it
A response continually increases the original change
A response occurs only after a voluntary decision
A response prevents all internal conditions from changing

questions.question: Which part of a neuron usually receives signals from other neurons?
In a typical neuron, in which direction does an action potential travel along the axon?
choices: From the cell body toward the axon terminals
From the axon terminals toward the dendrites only
From the myelin sheath into the nucleus
From the synaptic cleft into the cell body

questions.question: What is the main role of myelin around many axons?
choices: To increase the speed of impulse conduction
To release neurotransmitters into the blood
To detect changes in blood glucose

questions.question: At a chemical synapse, what is released from the presynaptic terminal to pass a signal across the synaptic cleft?
Which sequence correctly represents a basic reflex arc?
choices: Receptor, sensory neuron, integration centre, motor neuron, effector
Effector, sensory neuron, receptor, motor neuron, integration centre
Motor neuron, receptor, effector, sensory neuron, integration centre
Receptor, motor neuron, sensory neuron, effector, integration centre

questions.question: Which structure is primarily responsible for coordinating balance and fine control of movement?
Which brain region is especially important in regulating body temperature and hunger?
Which division of the autonomic nervous system generally prepares the body for rapid action?
Which response is generally associated with parasympathetic activity?
choices: Increased heart rate during a threat

questions.question: Which part of the eye changes its diameter to regulate how much light enters?
Which photoreceptors are especially important for colour vision in bright light?
Which structure in the inner ear contains receptors for detecting head rotation?
Which hormone lowers blood glucose by promoting its uptake and storage?
Which hormone is released by pancreatic alpha cells and tends to raise blood glucose?
Which gland produces thyroxine?
Which pituitary hormone stimulates the thyroid gland to release thyroid hormones?
Which hormone helps the kidneys conserve water by increasing water reabsorption in collecting ducts?
Which hormone is released from the adrenal medulla during an acute stress response?
Which hormone from the parathyroid glands raises blood calcium concentration?
Which hormone is most directly involved in stimulating uterine contractions during labour?
Which hormone primarily stimulates milk production after childbirth?
In a typical negative-feedback loop, what happens to secretion of a hormone when its regulated product rises sufficiently?
choices: The stimulus for further secretion is reduced
The hormone changes into an enzyme

questions.question: Which blood component is chiefly responsible for oxygen transport?
Which protein in red blood cells binds oxygen reversibly?
Which blood component initiates formation of a platelet plug at a damaged vessel?
Which plasma protein is converted into fibrin during blood clotting?
Which type of white blood cell can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells?
Which chamber of the heart pumps blood into the pulmonary artery?
Which chamber of the heart pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta?
Which valve prevents backflow from the left ventricle into the left atrium during ventricular contraction?
Which blood vessel carries blood from the right ventricle toward the lungs?
Which blood vessels return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
What is the usual sequence of blood flow through the heart after blood returns from the body?
choices: Right atrium, right ventricle, lungs, left atrium, left ventricle
Left atrium, left ventricle, lungs, right atrium, right ventricle
Right ventricle, right atrium, lungs, left ventricle, left atrium
Left ventricle, right ventricle, body, left atrium, lungs

questions.question: What is the main function of the sinoatrial node?
choices: It initiates the normal heartbeat rhythm
It filters waste from the blood
It prevents oxygen from entering the heart

questions.question: Which vessels have walls only one cell thick to support exchange with tissues?
Compared with veins, arteries generally have thicker muscular walls because they:
choices: Carry blood under higher pressure away from the heart
Always carry blood with more carbon dioxide
Contain valves at regular intervals throughout
Exchange most nutrients with body cells

questions.question: Which process moves oxygen from the alveoli into pulmonary capillary blood?
During quiet inhalation, what happens to the diaphragm?
choices: It pushes air directly into the blood

questions.question: Why does air enter the lungs during inhalation?
choices: Pressure inside the lungs falls below atmospheric pressure
Pressure inside the lungs rises above atmospheric pressure
Oxygen is actively pumped through the trachea

questions.question: Which feature of alveoli most directly supports rapid gas exchange?
choices: Large surface area and thin moist walls
Thick walls and a small surface area

questions.question: In which form is most carbon dioxide transported in human blood?
choices: Dissolved unchanged in red blood cells only

questions.question: What is the role of haemoglobin in carbon dioxide transport?
choices: Some carbon dioxide binds to haemoglobin
It converts all carbon dioxide directly into oxygen
It prevents carbon dioxide from leaving tissues
It transports carbon dioxide only in the lungs

questions.question: Which structure prevents food from entering the trachea during swallowing?
Where does most chemical digestion of starch begin?
Which enzyme begins protein digestion in the stomach?
What is the main digestive role of bile?
choices: Breaking proteins into amino acids by hydrolysis

questions.question: Where is bile produced?
What is a major digestive function of the pancreas?
choices: Secreting enzymes into the small intestine
Storing bile produced by the liver
Producing hydrochloric acid in the stomach

questions.question: Which region of the digestive tract is the main site of nutrient absorption?
What is the principal role of villi in the small intestine?
choices: Prevent all movement of intestinal contents

questions.question: Which nutrient is absorbed into lacteals in the villi mainly as part of chylomicrons?
Which structure carries absorbed glucose from the small intestine toward the liver?
What is peristalsis?
choices: Wave-like muscular contractions that move contents along the gut
The enzymatic breakdown of fats in the liver
The absorption of oxygen into blood
The filtration of blood in the kidney

questions.question: Which substance in the stomach provides an acidic environment that supports pepsin activity?
What is the main function of the large intestine?
choices: Absorption of water and electrolytes from remaining contents

questions.question: What is the functional unit of the kidney?
Where does filtration of blood plasma begin in a nephron?
Which substance is normally retained in the blood during glomerular filtration because of its size?
In a healthy kidney, where is most filtered glucose reabsorbed?
Which process returns useful substances from nephron fluid to the blood?
What is the principal nitrogen-containing waste product in human urine?
Which hormone increases water permeability in the kidney collecting ducts?
When a person is dehydrated, what change in urine is generally expected if the kidneys are functioning normally?
choices: No change in volume or concentration
Urine containing large numbers of red blood cells

questions.question: Which sequence correctly traces urine from the kidney to outside the body?
Which organ converts ammonia to urea?
Which structure carries urine from a kidney to the urinary bladder?
Which type of immunity is produced when a person's own immune system responds to an infection?
What is a primary function of antibodies?
Which cells can directly engulf and digest many invading microbes?
Which feature distinguishes adaptive immunity from innate immunity?
choices: Immediate response that is identical to every pathogen

questions.question: What is a key function of helper T cells in an adaptive immune response?
choices: Coordinate responses by signaling other immune cells

questions.question: Which cells are primarily responsible for destroying many virus-infected body cells?
Which structure produces sperm cells in the human male reproductive system?
Which hormone from the anterior pituitary stimulates sperm production indirectly by acting on Sertoli cells?
Which hormone stimulates Leydig cells in the testes to produce testosterone?
Where does fertilization most commonly occur in the human female reproductive tract?
Which hormone is released in a surge that triggers ovulation?
After ovulation, which ovarian structure produces progesterone during the luteal phase?
Which hormone helps maintain the uterine lining after ovulation?
Where does implantation of an early human embryo normally occur?
Which structure connects a developing fetus to the placenta and carries fetal blood between them?
Which statement best describes the role of the placenta?
choices: It allows exchange of substances between maternal and fetal blood
It produces sperm cells for the fetus
It directly pumps maternal blood through the fetal heart

questions.question: A person's blood glucose rises after a meal. Which response most directly helps return it toward its usual range?
A person moves from a warm room into a cold environment. Which response helps reduce heat loss from the skin?
Why does sweating help cool the body in a warm environment?
choices: Evaporation of sweat removes heat from the skin
Sweat permanently lowers the body's metabolic rate to zero
Sweat directly increases blood oxygen concentration
Sweat blocks all heat exchange with the surroundings

questions.question: Which muscle type is under voluntary control and is attached to bones?
Which muscle tissue forms the wall of the heart?
Which mineral ion is essential for initiating the interaction between actin and myosin during skeletal muscle contraction?
What is the main role of ATP in the muscle cross-bridge cycle?
choices: It allows myosin to detach from actin and supports cycling
It permanently locks myosin onto actin
It replaces calcium in the blood
It forms the muscle fibre's cell membrane

questions.question: Which joint type allows movement in many directions, as at the shoulder?
Which statement about oxygen delivery to body tissues is correct?
choices: Oxygen can dissociate from haemoglobin where tissue conditions favour its release
Haemoglobin releases oxygen only inside the stomach
Oxygen moves from tissues to blood by active transport in all cases
Red blood cells produce oxygen for surrounding tissues

questions.question: Which change in blood vessels would generally increase blood flow to a particular tissue, assuming other factors stay similar?
choices: Vasodilation of arterioles supplying the tissue
Closure of the tissue's venous drainage

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes ventilation from external gas exchange?
choices: Ventilation moves air; external gas exchange moves gases between alveoli and blood
Ventilation is blood filtration; external gas exchange is urine formation
Ventilation occurs only in blood; external gas exchange occurs only in the brain
The terms both mean oxygen production by red blood cells

questions.question: Which condition would most directly increase the rate of breathing through normal chemical control?
choices: A rise in carbon dioxide that lowers blood pH
A fall in body temperature during sleep
A rise in blood glucose after eating
A reduction in light entering the eye

questions.question: Which statement about the human urinary system is correct?
choices: The kidneys help regulate water and ion balance as well as remove wastes
The ureters filter blood into urine
The bladder produces urea from amino acids
The urethra carries blood from the heart to the kidneys

questions.question: What happens to the filtrate when useful water is reabsorbed from a nephron tubule into the blood?
choices: The remaining tubular fluid becomes more concentrated
The remaining tubular fluid becomes pure oxygen
The filtrate returns to the glomerulus unchanged

questions.question: Which structure in a villus transports absorbed water-soluble nutrients into the blood?
Which digestive enzyme breaks down triglycerides into smaller lipid products?
Which cells in the stomach lining secrete hydrochloric acid?
